q: Equilibrium means a state of _____.
e: Equilibrium means a state of balance. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: There are _____ types of equilibrium.
e: There are two types of equilibrium. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The two types of equilibrium are static equilibrium and _____ equilibrium.
e: The two types of equilibrium are static equilibrium and dynamic equilibrium. Chemical energy is stored in bonds.

q: A book at rest on a table is an example of _____ equilibrium.
e: A book at rest on a table is an example of static equilibrium. Chemical energy is stored in bonds.

q: The weight of a book gets balanced by the _____ reaction force from the table.
e: The weight of a book gets balanced by the normal reaction force from the table. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Both the forces are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction, resulting in _____ equilibrium.
e: Both the forces are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction, resulting in static equilibrium. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: All chemical reactions are _____ in nature.
e: All chemical reactions are dynamic in nature. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In a sealed bottle of soda, carbon dioxide is present in both the liquid phase and the _____ phase.
e: In a sealed bottle of soda, carbon dioxide is present in both the liquid phase and the gaseous phase. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Inside the sealed soda bottle, the gaseous carbon dioxide is turning into a liquid at the _____ rate that the liquid is turning back into a gas.
e: Inside the sealed soda bottle, the gaseous carbon dioxide is turning into a liquid at the same rate that the liquid is turning back into a gas. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The maintenance of equilibrium in reactions between haemoglobin and oxygen in human blood is one of the processes involving human _____.
e: The maintenance of equilibrium in reactions between haemoglobin and oxygen in human blood is one of the processes involving human health. Health: equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The carbon cycle contributes to the equilibrium process that minimises the impacts of _____ on the environment.
e: The carbon cycle contributes to the equilibrium process that minimises the impacts of carbon dioxide on the environment. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: A chemical equilibrium is a _____ equilibrium; that is, reactants are continuously being changed to products.
e: A chemical equilibrium is a dynamic equilibrium; that is, reactants are continuously being changed to products. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Many chemical reactions go to completion, meaning the products _____ be converted back to reactants.
e: Many chemical reactions go to completion, meaning the products cannot be converted back to reactants. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: There is the forward reaction where reactants are converted into products, and the _____ reaction where the products are converted back into the starting reactants.
e: There is the forward reaction where reactants are converted into products, and the reverse reaction where the products are converted back into the starting reactants. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: The symbol $\rightleftharpoons$ is used to represent the _____ reaction.
e: The symbol equilibrium is used to represent the reversible reaction. Exothermic means heat is given out and delta H is negative.

q: In the forward reaction, reactants A and B combine to form product C; in the reverse reaction, C _____ into A and B.
e: In the forward reaction, reactants A and B combine to form product C; in the reverse reaction, C decomposes into A and B. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: A reversible reaction is one that can occur in both the forward and reverse directions, and the conversions occur _____.
e: A reversible reaction is one that can occur in both the forward and reverse directions, and the conversions occur simultaneously. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: Reversible reactions that happen in a _____ system eventually reach equilibrium.
e: Reversible reactions that happen in a closed system eventually reach equilibrium. A reversible reaction can run forward and backward under the same conditions.

q: When the rates of the forward and reverse reactions balance, the reversible reaction is in _____.
e: When the rates of the forward and reverse reactions balance, the reversible reaction is in equilibrium. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions do not stop; rather, they continue to occur at the _____ rate.
e: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions do not stop; rather, they continue to occur at the same rate. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: After a system has reached equilibrium, the concentrations of all substances remain _____.
e: After a system has reached equilibrium, the concentrations of all substances remain constant. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Initially, the rate of the forward reaction is high and the rate of the reverse reaction is _____.
e: Initially, the rate of the forward reaction is high and the rate of the reverse reaction is low. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: As the reaction proceeds, the rate of the forward reaction decreases and the rate of the reverse reaction _____.
e: As the reaction proceeds, the rate of the forward reaction decreases and the rate of the reverse reaction increases. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: In homogenous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products are all in a single _____.
e: In homogenous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products are all in a single phase. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: In heterogeneous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products are present in more than one _____.
e: In heterogeneous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products are present in more than one phase. Heterogeneous means more than one phase is present.

q: A closed system is a system that allows energy to enter and exit, but matter can neither be gained nor _____.
e: A closed system is a system that allows energy to enter and exit, but matter can neither be gained nor lost. A closed system can exchange energy with the surroundings, but matter cannot enter or leave.

q: The reaction $N_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO(g)$ is an example of _____ chemical equilibrium.
e: The reaction N2(g) + O2(g) equilibrium 2NO(g) is an example of homogeneous chemical equilibrium. Heterogeneous means more than one phase.

q: The reaction $H_2O(l) \rightleftharpoons H_2O(g)$ is an example of _____ chemical equilibrium.
e: The reaction H2O(l) equilibrium H2O(g) is an example of heterogeneous chemical equilibrium. Homogeneous means the same phase.

q: Ammonium chloride breaks down when heated, forming ammonia and hydrogen chloride; this is a _____ reaction.
e: Ammonium chloride breaks down when heated, forming ammonia and hydrogen chloride; this is a reversible reaction. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: At dynamic equilibrium, the rates of forward and reverse reactions are _____.
e: At dynamic equilibrium, the rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: Le Chatelier's principle is a qualitative guide to the effect of changes in concentration, temperature, and pressure on a system at _____.
e: Le Chatelier's principle is a qualitative guide to the effect of changes in concentration, temperature, and pressure on a system at equilibrium. At equilibrium both directions still run, at equal rates.

q: Le Chatelier's principle was discovered by French Chemist Henri Louis Le Chatelier in the year _____.
e: Le Chatelier's principle was discovered by French Chemist Henri Louis Le Chatelier in the year 1884. Le Chatelier's principle says a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature.

q: If a system is in equilibrium and a factor is changed, the equilibrium shifts so as to _____ the effect of the change.
e: If a system is in equilibrium and a factor is changed, the equilibrium shifts so as to cancel out the effect of the change. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Once equilibrium is established in a system, no further change is apparent as long as the external factors remain _____.
e: Once equilibrium is established in a system, no further change is apparent as long as the external factors remain unchanged. Unchanged: equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: A change in concentration, temperature, or pressure makes a difference in the amount of product formed, however, a _____ does not affect the equilibrium concentrations.
e: A change in concentration, temperature, or pressure makes a difference in the amount of product formed, however, a catalyst does not affect the equilibrium concentrations. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Adding or removing a reactant or product from a reaction mixture at equilibrium will always _____ the equilibrium.
e: Adding or removing a reactant or product from a reaction mixture at equilibrium will always disturb the equilibrium. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: When the concentration of a reactant is increased, the reaction proceeds in the _____ direction in favour of products.
e: When the concentration of a reactant is increased, the reaction proceeds in the forward direction in favour of products. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: When the concentration of a reactant is decreased, the reaction proceeds in the reverse direction in favour of _____.
e: When the concentration of a reactant is decreased, the reaction proceeds in the reverse direction in favour of reactants. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: When the concentration of a product is increased, the equilibrium shifts to the _____ to reestablish equilibrium.
e: When the concentration of a product is increased, the equilibrium shifts to the left to reestablish equilibrium. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: When the concentration of a product is decreased, the equilibrium shifts to the _____ to reestablish equilibrium.
e: When the concentration of a product is decreased, the equilibrium shifts to the right to reestablish equilibrium. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: In the equilibrium $Fe^{3+}(aq) + SCN^-(aq) \rightleftharpoons FeSCN^{2+}(aq)$, the $Fe^{3+}$ ion in solution is pale _____.
e: In the equilibrium Fe3+(aq) + SCN-(aq) equilibrium FeSCN2+(aq), the Fe3+ ion in solution is pale yellow. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: In the same equilibrium, the $SCN^-$ ion in solution is _____.
e: In the same equilibrium, the SCN- ion in solution is colourless. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: In the same equilibrium, the colour of the $FeSCN^{2+}$ complex is blood _____.
e: In the same equilibrium, the colour of the FeSCN2+ complex is blood red. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The effect of temperature on chemical equilibrium depends upon the heat changes ($\Delta H$) of the reaction and follows _____ principle.
e: The effect of temperature on chemical equilibrium depends upon the heat changes (deltaH) of the reaction and follows Le Chatelier's principle. Le Chatelier's principle says a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature.

q: A temperature decrease favours an _____ reaction.
e: A temperature decrease favours an exothermic reaction. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: In the case of exothermic reactions, decreasing the temperature favours the exothermic reaction by _____ heat.
e: In the case of exothermic reactions, decreasing the temperature favours the exothermic reaction by releasing heat. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: In the case of endothermic reactions, increasing the temperature favours the endothermic reaction by _____ heat.
e: In the case of endothermic reactions, increasing the temperature favours the endothermic reaction by absorbing heat. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: In the decomposition of $N_2O_4$ to $NO_2$, the forward reaction is endothermic and the reverse reaction is _____.
e: In the decomposition of N2O4 to NO2, the forward reaction is endothermic and the reverse reaction is exothermic. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: When the temperature of the $N_2O_4$ and $NO_2$ mixture is decreased, the colour of the reaction mixture becomes _____.
e: When the temperature of the N2O4 and NO2 mixture is decreased, the colour of the reaction mixture becomes colourless. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: When the temperature of the $N_2O_4$ and $NO_2$ mixture is increased, the colour of the reaction mixture becomes _____.
e: When the temperature of the N2O4 and NO2 mixture is increased, the colour of the reaction mixture becomes reddish-brown. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: Pressure changes do not markedly affect the solid or liquid phases, however, pressure has a significant effect on the _____ phase.
e: Pressure changes do not markedly affect the solid or liquid phases, however, pressure has a significant effect on the gas phase. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: The pressure of a gas mixture at a given temperature is determined by the number of gas molecules in a given _____.
e: The pressure of a gas mixture at a given temperature is determined by the number of gas molecules in a given volume. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: If the pressure is increased, the position of equilibrium will shift towards the side with _____ moles of gas.
e: If the pressure is increased, the position of equilibrium will shift towards the side with fewer moles of gas. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: In chemical equilibrium, the change of pressure in both liquids and solids can be ignored because their volumes are independent of _____.
e: In chemical equilibrium, the change of pressure in both liquids and solids can be ignored because their volumes are independent of concentration. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: If the number of moles of gas is the same on both sides of the reversible chemical equation, pressure has _____ effect.
e: If the number of moles of gas is the same on both sides of the reversible chemical equation, pressure has no effect. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: In the synthesis of ammonia, the forward reaction is favoured at low temperature and _____ pressure.
e: In the synthesis of ammonia, the forward reaction is favoured at low temperature and high pressure. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: In the Haber process, there are four moles of reactants for every _____ moles of product formed.
e: In the Haber process, there are four moles of reactants for every two moles of product formed. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The catalyst used in the Haber process for ammonia production is iron(III) oxide with a small amount of _____ oxide.
e: The catalyst used in the Haber process for ammonia production is iron(III) oxide with a small amount of aluminium oxide. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Methanol is produced from carbon monoxide and _____ gas.
e: Methanol is produced from carbon monoxide and hydrogen gas. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The forward reaction for methanol production is exothermic, so decreasing the temperature will shift the position of equilibrium to the _____.
e: The forward reaction for methanol production is exothermic, so decreasing the temperature will shift the position of equilibrium to the right. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: The reaction for methanol production is carried out at a temperature of 250 °C using the catalyst _____.
e: The reaction for methanol production is carried out at a temperature of 250 °C using the catalyst Cu-ZnO-Al2O3. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Industrial processes are usually designed to give the maximum possible _____ of products.
e: Industrial processes are usually designed to give the maximum possible yield of products. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In 1864, two _____ chemists proposed the law of mass action as a general description of the equilibrium condition.
e: In 1864, two Norwegian chemists proposed the law of mass action as a general description of the equilibrium condition. Norwegian: equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: According to the law of mass action, for a reversible reaction at equilibrium and a constant temperature, the ratio between the concentration of reactants and products is _____.
e: According to the law of mass action, for a reversible reaction at equilibrium and a constant temperature, the ratio between the concentration of reactants and products is constant. A reversible reaction can run forward and backward under the same conditions.

q: The rate of the forward reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of the reactants raised to a power equal to their _____.
e: The rate of the forward reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of the reactants raised to a power equal to their coefficients. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: At equilibrium, the rates of forward and reverse reactions are _____.
e: At equilibrium, the rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: The ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations, with each raised to the power corresponding to its coefficient, is called the equilibrium _____.
e: The ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations, with each raised to the power corresponding to its coefficient, is called the equilibrium constant. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: The value of $K_{eq}$ is constant only at a specified _____.
e: The value of Keq is constant only at a specified temperature. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: Pure solids or liquids are _____ from the equilibrium expression because their concentrations remain constant.
e: Pure solids or liquids are excluded from the equilibrium expression because their concentrations remain constant. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: If the $K_{eq}$ value is large ($K_{eq} \gg 1$), the equilibrium lies to the right and there are more _____ than reactants.
e: If the Keq value is large (Keq1), the equilibrium lies to the right and there are more products than reactants. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: If the $K_{eq}$ value is small ($K_{eq} \ll 1$), the equilibrium lies to the _____ and there are more reactants than products.
e: If the Keq value is small (Keq1), the equilibrium lies to the left and there are more reactants than products. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: If the $K_{eq}$ value is equal to one, both reactants and products are equally favoured and their concentrations will be _____.
e: If the Keq value is equal to one, both reactants and products are equally favoured and their concentrations will be equal. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: For equilibrium that involves gases, the equilibrium constant $K_p$ can be given as the ratio of the partial _____ of products and reactants.
e: For equilibrium that involves gases, the equilibrium constant Kp can be given as the ratio of the partial pressures of products and reactants. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: In the equilibrium between ethanol(l) and ethanol(g), the equilibrium constant expression only includes the concentration of ethanol in the _____ state.
e: In the equilibrium between ethanol(l) and ethanol(g), the equilibrium constant expression only includes the concentration of ethanol in the gaseous state. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: The equilibrium for the sublimation of iodine crystals is an example of the solid-vapour _____ equilibrium state.
e: The equilibrium for the sublimation of iodine crystals is an example of the solid-vapour heterogeneous equilibrium state. Homogeneous means the same phase.

q: The equilibrium constant provides how far a reaction has gone towards _____ before it reaches equilibrium.
e: The equilibrium constant provides how far a reaction has gone towards completion before it reaches equilibrium. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: The units of equilibrium constant depend on the form of the equilibrium _____.
e: The units of equilibrium constant depend on the form of the equilibrium expression. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: In the reaction $HF(aq) \rightleftharpoons H^+(aq) + F^-(aq)$, the reaction is occurring in the _____.
e: In the reaction HF(aq) equilibrium H+(aq) + F-(aq), the reaction is occurring in the solution. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant is determined by measuring the concentration of each substance involved in a chemical reaction at _____.
e: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant is determined by measuring the concentration of each substance involved in a chemical reaction at equilibrium. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: Knowing the equilibrium constant expression, a chemist can calculate the equilibrium concentration of any substance if the concentrations of all other reactants and products are _____.
e: Knowing the equilibrium constant expression, a chemist can calculate the equilibrium concentration of any substance if the concentrations of all other reactants and products are known. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: In the decomposition of baking soda, the products include sodium carbonate, carbon dioxide, and _____.
e: In the decomposition of baking soda, the products include sodium carbonate, carbon dioxide, and water vapour. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The equilibrium constant is a ratio that expresses the relationship between the amounts of products and reactants present at equilibrium in a reversible chemical reaction at a given _____.
e: The equilibrium constant is a ratio that expresses the relationship between the amounts of products and reactants present at equilibrium in a reversible chemical reaction at a given temperature. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: When hot air and cold air are entering the room at the same time, the temperature of the room does not change at all, which is an example of _____ equilibrium in daily life.
e: When hot air and cold air are entering the room at the same time, the temperature of the room does not change at all, which is an example of dynamic equilibrium in daily life. Chemical energy is stored in bonds.

q: The transfer of $O_2$ from the lungs to the blood and then to the muscle tissues depends on the chemical equilibrium between oxygen and _____.
e: The transfer of O2 from the lungs to the blood and then to the muscle tissues depends on the chemical equilibrium between oxygen and water. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The equilibrium constant $K_c$ is used when molar _____ are used in the expression.
e: The equilibrium constant Kc is used when molar concentrations are used in the expression. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: Both $K_p$ and $K_c$ can be applied for the gaseous _____.
e: Both Kp and Kc can be applied for the gaseous reactions. Kp is the equilibrium constant written with partial pressures of gases.

q: In Example 1, increasing the concentration of $SCN^-$ ions shifts the equilibrium from left to right, making the colour of the solution a deep _____.
e: In Example 1, increasing the concentration of SCN- ions shifts the equilibrium from left to right, making the colour of the solution a deep red. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: In Example 2, the forward reaction for ammonia synthesis is an _____ (heat evolving) reaction.
e: In Example 2, the forward reaction for ammonia synthesis is an exothermic (heat evolving) reaction. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: In Example 3, increasing pressure on $2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2SO_3(g)$ favours the forward reaction because there are fewer moles of gas on the _____ side.
e: In Example 3, increasing pressure on 2SO2(g) + O2(g) equilibrium 2SO3(g) favours the forward reaction because there are fewer moles of gas on the product side. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: In Example 4, decreasing pressure on $4CuO(s) \rightleftharpoons 2Cu_2O(s) + O_2(g)$ favours the forward reaction because pressure affects only the _____ gas.
e: In Example 4, decreasing pressure on 4CuO(s) equilibrium 2Cu2O(s) + O2(g) favours the forward reaction because pressure affects only the oxygen gas. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: In Example 5, increasing pressure on $H_2(g) + I_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HI(g)$ has _____ effect because the number of moles of reactants is equal to that of the product.
e: In Example 5, increasing pressure on H2(g) + I2(g) equilibrium 2HI(g) has no effect because the number of moles of reactants is equal to that of the product. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Hydrogen and bromine reversibly react to form _____.
e: Hydrogen and bromine reversibly react to form HBr. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In the reaction $H_2(g) + Br_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HBr(g)$, changing the pressure does not affect the amount of product because the moles of gas are _____ on both sides.
e: In the reaction H2(g) + Br2(g) equilibrium 2HBr(g), changing the pressure does not affect the amount of product because the moles of gas are equal on both sides. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: Ammonia is prepared from nitrogen and _____.
e: Ammonia is prepared from nitrogen and hydrogen. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: To obtain more $HCl$ in the equilibrium $2Cl_2(g) + 2H_2O(g) \rightleftharpoons 4HCl(g) + O_2(g)$ which is endothermic, the temperature should be _____.
e: To obtain more HCl in the equilibrium 2Cl2(g) + 2H2O(g) equilibrium 4HCl(g) + O2(g) which is endothermic, the temperature should be increased. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: In the equilibrium $CO(g) + 2H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons CH_3OH(g)$, if $K_{eq} = 10.5$, the equilibrium lies to the _____.
e: In the equilibrium CO(g) + 2H2(g) equilibrium CH3OH(g), if Keq = 10.5, the equilibrium lies to the right.

q: For the reaction $CH_3COOC_2H_5(aq) + H_2O(l) \rightleftharpoons CH_3COOH(aq) + C_2H_5OH(aq)$, the water is excluded from the $K_c$ expression because it is a pure _____.
e: For the reaction CH3COOC2H5(aq) + H2O(l) equilibrium CH3COOH(aq) + C2H5OH(aq), the water is excluded from the Kc expression because it is a pure liquid. Kc uses equilibrium concentrations, and its value changes only if you change the temperature.

q: In the reaction $Cd^{2+}(aq) + 4Br^-(aq) \rightleftharpoons CdBr_4^{2-}(aq)$, the equilibrium constant expression has the product concentration raised to the power of _____.
e: In the reaction Cd2+(aq) + 4Br-(aq) equilibrium CdBr42-(aq), the equilibrium constant expression has the product concentration raised to the power of 1. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: In the reaction $CH_4(g) + 2H_2S(g) \rightleftharpoons CS_2(l) + 4H_2(g)$, the $CS_2$ is excluded from the equilibrium expression because it is a _____.
e: In the reaction CH4(g) + 2H2S(g) equilibrium CS2(l) + 4H2(g), the CS2 is excluded from the equilibrium expression because it is a liquid. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The synthesis of ammonia (Haber process) is a good example of an industrial process that uses _____ principle.
e: The synthesis of ammonia (Haber process) is a good example of an industrial process that uses Le Chatelier's principle. Le Chatelier's principle says a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature.

q: When running on a treadmill, the person is moving forwards, and the treadmill is moving backward at the _____ rate, illustrating dynamic equilibrium.
e: When running on a treadmill, the person is moving forwards, and the treadmill is moving backward at the same rate, illustrating dynamic equilibrium. At dynamic equilibrium the forward and reverse reactions still run, but they run at the same rate so concentrations stay constant.
